He could use telekinesis in many ways, such as pulling a lightsaber to his hand or drawing a Sith amulet into his hand from across a grand hall.<ref name="dlots1" /><ref name="dlots3" /><ref name="dlots4" /> As a Sith Lord he could use [[Telekinesis/Legends|Force Wound]] to destroy the internal organs of foes, hurl people and items away from himself, and create small [[Telekinesis/Legends|whirlwinds]] to buffet, trap, or harm people.<ref name="kotorcg" /> He also was able to use the Force pull/disarm technique&mdash;as demonstrated when he ripped the [[Dark Holocron]] from the hand of Odan-Urr.<ref name="tsw1" /> Kun was able to fling Sylvar away with ease.<ref name="tsw3" /> Kun could raise the ''[[Corsair (Derriphan-class)|Corsair]]'' with his telekinetic might.<ref name="kotorcg">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> His defenses against telekinesis were not perfect, however, as [[Odan-Urr/Legends|Odan-Urr]] subjected him to a Force strike upon the Sith's theft of the [[Holocron/Legends|Holocron]].<ref name="tsw1" />

Kun would develop strong mental Force powers, like the [[Mind trick/Legends|Mind Trick]],<ref name="dss" /> notably using a [[Qâzoi Kyantuska|Sith spell to mesmerize the entire Galactic Senate and dominate the mind]] of the Supreme Chancellor&mdash;forcing him to preach Sith philosophy to all who were listening. Kun's sorcery could be used to [[Injure/Kill|slay]] those who he touched and broke the minds of.<ref name="tsw3" /> Kun was unfazed by the [[Mind trick/Legends|Sith illusions]] Keto tired to use to stop him.<ref name="dlots6" /> Kun could [[Comprehend Speech|learn how to speak a tounge]] by [[Drain Knowledge|stealing the knowledge]] from another's mind. His telepathic abilities occasionally extended to the reaches of the galaxy, while bearing his Sith amulet, as in his attempt to eliminate potential rivals he was able to detect other Sith practitioners in the galaxy.<ref name="kotorII" /> Kun could [[Force Stasis/Legends|stun]] his rivals, and use the [[Tutaminis|Force to resist energy]].<ref name="kotorcg" /> Also, he he was merely knocked back by Jedi Master Odan-Urr's combination of a Force strike and Sever Force, and the Jedi Master unable to kill off the Sith's [[Midi-chlorian/Legends|Midi-chlorians]].<ref name="tsw1" /> Kun may have [[Force healing/Legends|healed]] himself of his bones being broken in one hundred places, though it is not clear if he did the healing or the the ghost of Nadd preformed the dark healing.<ref name="dlots3" /> Exar Kun had great skill with the [[Force blast|Force Blast]] power, using it in the thores of his rage (while wearing a Sith amulet and boosted by the power of a Sith Temple) to kill a huge Sith wyrm and slaughter Massassi, before destroying the Force Ghost of Freedon Nadd.<ref name="dlots4" /> Later he effortlessly knocked out [[Aleema Keto]] with a Force blast.<ref name="dlots6" /> On Yavin 4, Kun intensely studied Sith sorcery, learning how to unleash enormous amounts of destructive dark side energy with alchemy and sith machines,<ref name="dlots4" /> even more so once he discovered Naga Sadow's ancient ''Corsair''.<ref name="tsw4" /> Kun understood how to use the Sith ship to [[Supernova (Sith magic)|wrench fire from the stars]], though he never used this function of the ship in battle.<ref name="tsw4" /> The discovery of the ''Corsair'' also allowed Kun to research [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]],<ref name="dlots5" /> which he would quickly master&mdash;Kun would eventually gain the ability to create monstrous dark side creatures, such as terentateks and Sith wyrms, that would continue to pose a menace long after the end of the Great Sith War.<ref name="nec" /> Kun was able to [[Force drain|drain]] vitality from his opponents, either to [[Force healing|heal]] himself or simply to reduce their [[personal Force reservoir]].<ref name="kotorcg" /> When he delved deeper into Sith sorcery, Kun discovered pathways that he did not truly understand, but that he used anyway to [[Force ghost/Legends|free himself of his body]]&mdash;via power of the Sith temple and magical site within&mdash;at the end of the Sith War&mdash;at the [[Death/Legends|expense]] of thousands of Massassi lives.<ref name="tsw6" />

[[File:ExarVsUlic.jpg|thumb|250px|Exar Kun battles Ulic Qel-Droma in the Iron Citadel.]]

But while he would become a master of the arcane ways of the dark side,<ref name="nec" /> Exar Kun shone the most with his vaunted lightsaber ability, which he honed in training duels with the Cathar Crado and Sylvar on Dantooine.<ref name="dlots1" /> His preferred form was [[Form VI/Legends|Niman]].<ref name="kotorcg" /> Kun was also capable in the use of the [[Jar'Kai/Legends|Jar'Kai]] style.<ref name="dlots1" /><ref name="tsw2" /> Even as an apprentice, Kun was strong enough to defeat his Master, Vodo-Siosk Baas, although his combat style tapped into an inner anger that worried his Master. An overwhelming combatant with his single-bladed lightsaber,<ref name="dlots1" /> Kun would later add to his arsenal by innovating and mastering the double-bladed lightsaber, which was a previously unseen weapon in his time.<ref name="tsw3" /> Kun's formidable prowess in combat was bolstered by his tactical genius in utilizing the adaptability of his double-bladed lightsaber. By suddenly changing the intensity or length of one of his blades, Kun was often able to trick his opponents into overextending themselves and creating openings for fatal counterstrikes. Coupling his tactics with his ability to predict his enemies' actions through the Force, Kun became a nearly unbeatable force.<ref name="wat">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> However, Kun admitted that he could not defeat the whole Jedi Order gathered to fight him at once.<ref name="tsw6" />

In addition to his proficiency with a lightsaber, Kun was also handy with a [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]] and with [[Vibro-weapon/Legends|vibroweapons]]. Kun was fluent in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], [[Arkanian (language)/Legends|Arkanian]], [[Twi'leki/Legends|Ryl]],<ref name="dss" /> [[Catharese]], [[Kreva]], and [[Tetan/Legends|Tetan]],<ref name="kotorcg" /> along with the ancient Sith language after his corruption to the dark side at the hands of Freedon Nadd. Kun was a strong and ruthless leader&mdash;able to command the Massassi with ease once he proved his dark side loyalty and might.<ref name="dlots4" /><ref name="tsw2" /> Moreover, Kun was a canny speaker and liar, able to inspire many Jedi to follow him into darkness with his half-truths and deceits&mdash;even convincing those who entered the room where he murdered Odan-Urr that the old master had died of old age. These tricks were enough to get twenty Jedi to follow him to Yavin 4 and into darkness.<ref name="tsw1" /><ref name="tsw2" /> Once he converted the Jedi under his sway to the dark side, the willingly (per their magically twisted mindsets) went out to kill their masters.<ref name="tsw3" /> Moreover, Kun recovered from being thrown into a chair by the telekinetic attack of Odan-Urr and then got back up and fatally wounded the Jedi Master with his own dark side powers.<ref name="tsw1" /> Kun was a fair [[Architect/Legends|architect]], at least able to manage projects of grand scale and organize the creation of hundreds of dark side temples that would last for thousands of years.<ref name="dlots4" /><ref name="tsw3" /> However, it should be noted that he was following Naga Sadow's plans and had very loyal builders.<ref name="dlots4" />

Kun's powers expanded after his physical death, although he lost the ability to use some Force skills, such as [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]]. No longer bound to a mortal body, Kun gained the ability to manifest where he pleased amongst his network of temples on Yavin 4,<ref name="dss" /> appear in the minds of others,<ref name="apprentice" /> and even possess his targets.<ref name="dss" /> In his spiritual form, Kun was still strong enough to complete great feats of Force power, such as sundering Luke Skywalker's spirit from his body and helping Kyp Durron bring forth the Sun Crusher from Yavin's sun,<ref name="apprentice" /> but he was weak enough that he was unable to prevent his own demise at the hands of a group of Jedi apprentices.<ref name="champions" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|Time to make this more interesting&hellip; do you like the modifications I made to my lightsaber, Master?|Exar Kun unveils his double-bladed lightsaber|<ref name="tsw3" />}}
[[File:ExarAttacks.jpg|thumb|250px|Exar Kun wields his double-bladed lightsaber.|left]]
A master of lightsaber combat, Exar Kun was remembered for his innovation of the double-bladed lightsaber,<ref name="wat" /> using a [[Color/Legends|blue]]-bladed weapon<ref name="tsw3" /> that he constructed himself as a modification of his original blue-bladed lightsaber.<ref name="wat" /> Although Kun was often credited with the weapon's invention, Master Vodo-Siosk Baas' Tedryn Holocron stated that Kun followed instructions from a Sith holocron, possibly prepared by the original Sith Lords, Jedi exiles who fought in the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]] millennia before Kun's life.<ref name="jvs" /> Kun added a second emitter matrix on the other end of the lightsaber's handle,<ref name="wat" /> which allowed him to use the weapon with only one blade released or both.<ref name="tsw3" /> Kun also added customized controls to the lightsaber, allowing him to adjust both the length&mdash;measuring from half a meter to one and a half meters&mdash;and the intensity of each blade, using this variability to his tactical advantage in combat. Kun used this modified lightsaber much as his Master, Vodo-Siosk Baas, used his [[Quarterstaff/Legends|quarterstaff]], utilizing one blade to block attacks before spinning his grip and attacking with the other blade.<ref name="wat" />

Kun's lightsaber prowess and Force ability was bolstered in turn by the powerful Sith amulet that he obtained after being captured by the Massassi on his first trip to Yavin 4. Wearing the amulet on his left hand and shoulder, Kun gained the ability to unleash huge amounts of dark side energy.<ref name="dlots4" /> Kun owned a [[Cortosis/Legends|cortosis]]-woven<ref name="bigredone">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20040722yavin|text=Yavin: The Big Red One|int=Yavin: The Big Red One}}</ref> [[Exar Kun's light battle suit|light battle suit]] during his life, which may have been found by the Sith-turned-Jedi [[Revan/Legends|Revan]]<ref name="kotor" /> and his fellow Jedi [[Meetra Surik]] on their adventures during the Jedi Civil War and [[Dark Wars]], respectively.<ref name="kotorII" /> Not long after the Battle of Yavin, the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] treasure hunter [[Suz Tanwa]] discovered what she believed to be Kun's light battle suit on the moon of [[Yavin 22]], where it had been hidden by her ancestor, [[Suvam Tan]], a former Sith slave during the Great Sith War.<ref name="bigredone" /> During his life, Kun made use of his personal starship, the ''[[Starstorm One]]'', a vessel that could be operated by himself alone.<ref name="dlots2" /> Kun used the ''Starstorm One'' as a Jedi apprentice and continued to fly the ship as Dark Lord of the Sith, using it to transport Jedi artifacts after his raid on Ossus.<ref name="tsw5" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I almost wish I could have done the backstory first. I could've added more detail to the books. I spent more time writing the comics than the books. I know so much about him; he wouldn't have been quite so clear-cut a villain. I'd take the edge off him.|Kevin J. Anderson|<ref name="comicscan">{{GalaxyCite|8|ComicScan|ComicScan: Taken by Force}}</ref>}}
[[File:KunActionFigure.jpg|thumb|300px|Exar Kun in action figure form]]
The character of Exar Kun was created by author [[Kevin J. Anderson]],<ref name="lucasfilm22">[[The Lucasfilm Fan Club Magazine 22|''The Lucasfilm Fan Club Magazine'' 22]]</ref> who used the Dark Lord's spirit as a major antagonist of his [[1994]] [[Star Wars: The Jedi Academy Trilogy|''Jedi Academy Trilogy'']]. Kun was first mentioned as a dreamlike "dark man" in a vision described in the trilogy's first novel, ''[[Jedi Search]]'',<ref name="search" /> and was properly introduced in the next novel, [[Dark Apprentice (novel)|''Dark Apprentice'']].<ref name="apprentice" /> When creating the character, Anderson was initially unsure whether Kun should be a Dark Lord of the Sith or a "[[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]],"<ref name="lucasfilm22" /> finally making his decision when [[George Lucas]] voted on the former.<ref name="comicscan" /> Soon afterward, [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi (comic series)|''Tales of the Jedi'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] author [[Tom Veitch]] suggested that they combine Kun's story with that of Veitch's already-running ''Tales of the Jedi'', as Kun had only been established as living "sometime in the past" and not in any set timeframe.<ref name="lucasfilm22" /> Enthusiastic about the idea, Anderson decided to sketch out Kun's backstory for a stand-alone ''Tales of the Jedi'' issue, which turned into a three-issue story arc, which ended up turning into the 12 issues comprising [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith|''Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi - Dark Lords of the Sith'']]&mdash;written by a collaboration between Veitch and Anderson&mdash;and ''[[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War]]'', written by Anderson alone.<ref name="lucasfilm22" />

[[File:ExarKun-NEGTC.png|thumb|left|180px|Exar Kun, Dark Lord of the Sith]]
After writing the comics and fleshing out Kun's life story, Anderson stated that he wished he could have written the ''Jedi Academy Trilogy'' books afterward, as he had a better sense of the character and he could have provided more depth.<ref name="comicscan" /> In the ''Star Wars'' universe, Kun is notable as the first character ever depicted wielding a double-bladed lightsaber, a weapon that would gain popularity when the antagonist Darth Maul used it in the [[1999]] movie [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="menace">{{InsiderCite|109|Menace Revisited}}</ref> The concept was created by artist [[Chris Gossett]], who pencilled most of the ''Dark Lords of the Sith'' arc, but it went unused until fellow artist [[Dario Carrasco, Jr.]] drew Kun with it in ''Tales of the Jedi: The Sith War''.<ref name="insider153">{{InsiderCite|153|Authors of the Expanded Universe|Authors of the Expanded Universe: ''Tales'' of the ''Sith''}}</ref> During his run in the ''Tales of the Jedi'' comics, Kun was illustrated by three different artists: Gossett,<ref name="dlots1" /> Carrasco,<ref name="tsw1" /> and [[Art Wetherell]].<ref name="dlots6" /> Kun was also portrayed in the [[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|audio adaptation]] of ''Dark Lords of the Sith'', where he was voiced by [[Peter Renaday|Peter Reneday]].<ref name="audio" />''<nowiki/>''

The [[Star Wars Insider 26|''Star Wars Insider'' 26]] article [[The Horse's Mouth|''Straight from the Horse's Mouth'']] lists Kun's rise to Dark Lord of the Sith at 3991 BBY,<ref name="insider26">{{InsiderCite|26|The Horse's Mouth|Straight from the Horse's Mouth: A Guide to the ''Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi'' Universe, Part 1}}</ref> although numerous later sources place the event at 3997 BBY.<ref name="nec" /> As the ''Insider'' article contradicts numerous other established dates, it is treated as incorrect on that matter for the purposes of this article.
